items.name: Spec compliance
items.note: Operator chose 'Accept + note' for all three decisions (old anon key, 2 react-router CVEs, 2 build-time glob/minimatch CVEs). Each finding is suppressed by an exact identifier with a written reachability statement; plugin scan now 0 findings with all 3 classes covered.

items.name: Security basics
items.note: Suppressions are narrow: gitleaks by full fingerprint (commit:file:rule:line), so a new JWT anywhere else still fails; trivy by exact CVE id with exp:2027-05-01, verified an expired entry resurfaces. No secret value is written in either file (fingerprint only). Reachability checked in code: all Link targets literal, HashRouter SPA without SSR, glob/minimatch only via tailwindcss>sucrase at build time.

items.name: Test quality
items.note: Verified empirically: CI-style `trivy fs .` -> 0 vulns; gitleaks with history -> no leaks; plugin run_scan_and_report -> 0 findings; expiry probe resurfaces CVE. Unit suite unchanged (behavior snapshot).

items.name: Naming & structure
items.note: Flat .trivyignore chosen over .trivyignore.yaml because CI runs plain `trivy fs .` (v0.74 default ignorefile is .trivyignore only); plugin also reads it. .gitleaksignore is gitleaks' auto-loaded file.

items.name: Affected boundaries
items.note: Consumers: local OSS scan (plugin passes --ignorefile / gitleaks -s root) and CI security.yml (trivy fs . from root; gitleaks --no-git, where the history-only JWT never appears). Both verified.
